paragraphs: We are a biotechnology company developing and commercializing life-changing therapies for people living with gastrointestinal, or GI, and rare diseases. We are focused on the development and commercialization of innovative product opportunities in areas of significant unmet need, leveraging our demonstrated expertise and capabilities in GI and rare diseases.

LINZESS® (linaclotide), our commercial product, is the first product approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration, or U.S. FDA, in a class of GI medicines called guanylate cyclase type C agonists, or GC-C agonists, and is indicated for the treatment, in the U.S., of irritable bowel syndrome with constipation, or IBS-C, in adults and pediatric patients 7 years of age and older, chronic idiopathic constipation, or CIC, in adults, and functional constipation, or FC, in pediatric patients ages 6-17 years-old. LINZESS is also available for the treatment of adults with IBS-C or CIC in Mexico, adults with IBS-C or chronic constipation in Japan, and adults with IBS-C in China. Linaclotide is available under the trademarked name CONSTELLA® for the treatment of adults with IBS-C or CIC and pediatric patients ages 6-17 years old with FC in Canada, and to adults with IBS-C in certain European countries.

We have strategic partnerships with leading pharmaceutical companies to support the development and commercialization of linaclotide throughout the world, including with our partner, AbbVie Inc. (together with its affiliates), or AbbVie, in the U.S. and all countries worldwide other than China (including Hong Kong and Macau) and Japan, AstraZeneca AB (together with its affiliates), or AstraZeneca, in China (including Hong Kong and Macau) and Astellas Pharma Inc., or Astellas, in Japan.

Through our acquisition of VectivBio Holding AG, or VectivBio, in June 2023, or the VectivBio Acquisition, we are advancing apraglutide, a next-generation, synthetic long-acting peptide analog of glucagon-like peptide-2, or GLP-2, for short bowel syndrome, or SBS, patients who are dependent on parenteral support, or PS. In February 2024, we announced positive topline results from our pivotal Phase III clinical trial, STARS, which evaluated the efficacy and safety of once-weekly subcutaneous apraglutide in reducing PS dependency in adult patients with short bowel syndrome with intestinal failure, or SBS-IF. We are also conducting an open-label extension study, STARS Extend, to further assess the safety of apraglutide in adult patients with SBS-IF. In April 2025, we announced that, based on discussions with the U.S. FDA, a confirmatory Phase III clinical trial is needed to seek approval of a new drug application or NDA, for apraglutide for patients with SBS-IF who are dependent on PS. In the fourth quarter of 2025, we met with the U.S. FDA and aligned on key design elements of a confirmatory Phase III clinical trial, STARS-2, of apraglutide. Site initiations are expected to begin in the second quarter of 2026.

We were incorporated in Delaware on January 5, 1998 as Microbia, Inc. On April 7, 2008, we changed our name to Ironwood Pharmaceuticals, Inc. To date, we have dedicated a majority of our activities to the research, development and commercialization of linaclotide, as well as other research and development programs, including apraglutide.

Drug development involves a high degree of risk and investment, and the status, timing and scope of our development programs are subject to change. Important factors that could adversely affect our drug development efforts are discussed under the heading "Risk Factors" in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

In 2025, our GI and rare diseases-focused strategy, building on our commercial success and GI development capabilities, continued to focus on three core priorities: maximizing LINZESS, advancing apraglutide, and delivering sustained profits and cash flow.

● We recognized $289.3 million in collaborative arrangements revenue related to sales of LINZESS in the U.S. during the year ended December 31, 2025, a decrease of $51.1 million compared to the year ended
December 31, 2024. The decrease was driven by net price and inventory channel fluctuations, partially offset by increased prescription demand.

● In April 2025, we announced that, in preparation for the NDA submission to the U.S. FDA for apraglutide, pharmacokinetic analysis indicated that the exposure and dose delivered in the STARS Phase III clinical trial were lower than planned due to dose preparation and administration. Based on discussions with the U.S. FDA, it became clear that a confirmatory Phase III clinical trial of apraglutide is needed to seek approval of an NDA for apraglutide for patients with SBS-IF who are dependent on PS. In the fourth quarter of 2025, we met with the U.S. FDA and aligned on key design elements of a confirmatory Phase III clinical trial, STARS-2, of apraglutide. We plan to initiate the STARS-2 clincial trial in the second quarter of 2026.
Delivering sustained profits and cash flow
● We generated $127.0 million in cash from operations during the year ended December 31, 2025, ending the year with $215.5 million in cash and cash equivalents.

IBS-C and CIC are chronic, functional GI disorders that afflict millions of sufferers worldwide. As many as 11.5 million adults suffer from IBS-C and as many as 28.5 million adults suffer from CIC in the U.S., based on Rome II criteria from the Lieberman GI Patient Landscape Survey performed in 2010, or the Lieberman Survey. Symptoms of IBS-C include abdominal pain, discomfort and/or bloating and constipation symptoms (e.g., incomplete evacuation, infrequent bowel movements, hard/lumpy stools), while CIC is primarily characterized by constipation symptoms. Greater than 65% of IBS-C patients suffer from bloating and/or discomfort at least one time per week, according to the Lieberman Survey.

Linaclotide—U.S. In August 2012, the U.S. FDA approved LINZESS as a once daily treatment for adults suffering from IBS-C (290 mcg dose) or CIC (145 mcg dose). We and AbbVie began commercializing LINZESS in the U.S. in December 2012. In January 2017, the U.S. FDA approved a 72 mcg dose of linaclotide for the treatment of adults with CIC in the U.S.

headings: Risks Related to LINZESS, Apraglutide and Other Product Candidates
We are highly dependent on the commercial success of LINZESS (linaclotide) in the U.S. for the foreseeable future.
Healthcare reform and other governmental and private payor initiatives may have an adverse effect upon, and could prevent, our products' or product candidates' commercial success.
We cannot give any assurance that apraglutide will receive regulatory approval, which is necessary before it can be commercialized.
Our failure to successfully develop and commercialize additional product candidates or approved products would impair our ability to grow and/or adversely affect our business.
Delays in the completion of clinical testing of any of our products or product candidates could result in increased costs and could delay or limit our ability to generate revenues.
The pricing of apraglutide and our other product candidates, if and when approved for marketing, will depend in part on pricing and reimbursement strategies adopted by our competitors.
We face competition and new products may emerge that provide different or better alternatives for treatment of the conditions that our products are approved to treat.

Even though linaclotide is approved for marketing in the U.S. and in a number of other countries, we or our partners may never receive approval to commercialize linaclotide in additional parts of the world.

If we are unable to successfully partner with other companies to develop and commercialize products and/or product candidates, our ability to grow would be impaired and our business would be adversely affected.
Risks Related to the VectivBio Acquisition
We may not realize the expected benefits and anticipated synergies of the VectivBio Acquisition.
paragraphs: In addition to the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, any of the factors described below could significantly and negatively affect our business, financial condition, results of operations or prospects. The trading price of our Class A Common Stock may decline due to these risks.

We and our partner, AbbVie, began selling LINZESS in the U.S. in December 2012. Revenues from our LINZESS collaboration constitute a significant portion of our total revenue, and we believe they will continue to do so for the foreseeable future. The commercial success of LINZESS depends on a number of factors, including:
● the effectiveness of LINZESS as a treatment in the approved indications; ● the size of the treatable patient population;
● the effectiveness of the sales, managed markets and marketing efforts, including the ability to adapt a commercial model and market strategy to the evolving landscape;
● the coverage and reimbursement levels set by governmental authorities, private health insurers and other third-party payors;
● the status of government regulation in the life sciences industry, particularly with respect to healthcare reform and drug pricing;

paragraphs: 本公司為一生物科技公司，致力於開發及商業化對患有消化道，或稱 GI，及罕見疾病的患者具有改變生命的療法。本公司專注於開發及商業化創新產品機會，以解決重大未被滿足的醫療需求，並運用本公司在 GI 及罕見疾病領域所展示的專業知識與能力。

LINZESS®（linaclotide）為本公司之商業產品，為美國食品藥物管理局，或稱 U.S. FDA，批准的第一款屬於 GI 藥物類別中稱為 guanylate cyclase type C agonists，或 GC-C agonists 的藥物，並於美國用於治療成人及年滿 7 歲之兒童之腸易激綜合症伴隨便祕，或 IBS-C，慢性特發性便祕，或 CIC，以及 6 至 17 歲兒童之功能性便祕，或 FC。LINZESS 亦於墨西哥用於治療 IBS-C 或 CIC 之成人，日本用於治療 IBS-C 或慢性便祕之成人，以及中國用於治療 IBS-C 之成人。linaclotide 在加拿大以 CONSTELLA® 商標名稱用於治療 IBS-C 或 CIC 之成人及 6 至 17 歲之兒童 FC，並在某些歐洲國家用於治療 IBS-C 之成人。
本公司與領先的製藥公司有戰略合作關係，以支持 linaclotide 在全球的開發與商業化，包括與我們的合作夥伴 AbbVie Inc.（與其附屬公司合稱）或 AbbVie，在美國及全球所有國家（包括香港及澳門）與日本，AstraZeneca AB（與其附屬公司合稱）或 AstraZeneca，在中國（包括香港及澳門）與 Astellas Pharma Inc.，或 Astellas，在日本。

透過我們於 2023 年 6 月收購 VectivBio Holding AG，或 VectivBio，或稱 VectivBio 收購，我們正在推進 apraglutide，一種新一代的合成長效肽類模擬物，為 glucagon-like peptide-2，或 GLP-2，的藥物，用於依賴靜脈營養支持，或 PS 的短腸綜合症，或 SBS 患者。於 2024 年 2 月，我們宣佈在評估 once-weekly subcutaneous apraglutide 在減少成人短腸綜合症伴隨腸道功能衰竭，或 SBS-IF 患者 PS 依賴性的關鍵 III 期臨牀試驗 STARS 中取得正面的初步結果。我們亦正在進行一項開放標籤延長試驗 STARS Extend，以進一步評估 apraglutide 在 SBS-IF 成人患者中的安全性。於 2025 年 4 月，我們宣佈，根據與美國食品藥物管理局的討論，為尋求批准新藥申請，或 NDA，用於依賴 PS 的 SBS-IF 患者，需進行確認性 III 期臨牀試驗。於 2025 年第四季，我們與美國食品藥物管理局會面，並就確認性 III 期臨牀試驗 STARS-2 的關鍵設計要素達成共識。預計於 2026 年第二季開始進行試驗場地啟動。
本公司於 1998 年 1 月 5 日在特拉華州註冊成立，名為 Microbia, Inc. 於 2008 年 4 月 7 日，本公司更名為 Ironwood Pharmaceuticals, Inc. 至今，本公司已將大部分活動投入於 linaclotide 的研究、開發與商業化，以及其它研究與開發計畫，包括 apraglutide。
藥物開發涉及高度風險與投資，且本公司開發計畫的狀態、時間與範圍可能有所變動。影響本公司藥物開發努力的重要因素，於本年度報告表 10-K 中的「風險因素」標題下有討論。
於 2025 年，本公司聚焦於 GI 及罕見疾病的策略，建立在商業成功與 GI 開發能力之上，持續著重於三個核心優先事項：最大化 LINZESS，推進 apraglutide，並實現持續的獲利與現金流。

2024年12月31日。減幅係因淨價格及存貨通路波動，部分抵銷處方需求增加。

● 2025年4月，我們宣佈，為準備向美國FDA提交apraglutide的NDA申請，藥代動力學分析顯示，在STARS第三期臨牀試驗中，因劑量準備及給藥過程，暴露量與實際施打劑量低於預期。根據與美國FDA的討論，已明確需進行apraglutide的確認性第三期臨牀試驗，以尋求apraglutide用於依賴PS的SBS-IF患者的NDA批准。2025年第四季，我們與美國FDA會面，並就apraglutide的確認性第三期臨牀試驗STARS-2的設計要點達成共識。我們預計於2026年第二季啟動STARS-2臨牀試驗。
持續創造穩定獲利與現金流

IBS-C及CIC為慢性、功能性消化道疾病，影響全球數百萬患者。根據2010年進行的Lieberman GI Patient Landscape Survey（Lieberman調查）所採用的Rome II準則，美國有高達11.5百萬成人罹患IBS-C，高達28.5百萬成人罹患CIC。IBS-C的症狀包括腹部疼痛、不適與/或脹氣以及便祕症狀（例如：排便不完全、排便次數減少、硬便/塊狀便），而CIC則主要以便祕症狀為特徵。根據Lieberman調查，超過65%的IBS-C患者每週至少有一次脹氣與/或不適的症狀。
Linaclotide—美國。2012年8月，美國FDA批准LINZESS作為每日一次治療，用於罹患IBS-C（290 mcg劑量）或CIC（145 mcg劑量）的成人。我們與AbbVie於2012年12月開始在美國商業化LINZESS。2017年1月，美國FDA批准72 mcg劑量的linaclotide，用於治療美國罹患CIC的成人。

● 本公司於2025年12月31日財年認列總收入296.2百萬美元，較2024年12月31日財年之351.4百萬美元減少。減少主要為美國銷售LINZESS之淨利潤分享減少51.1百萬美元，此為淨價格下降及存貨通路波動所致，部分抵銷因處方需求增加所帶來之影響。此外，2024年12月31日財年結果包含因銷售預備金及允許金額之估計變動，導致協作收入減少43.0百萬美元。

headings: 與 LINZESS、Apraglutide 及其他產品候選藥物相關的風險
我們在可預見的未來高度依賴 LINZESS（linaclotide）在美國的商業成功。
醫療改革及其他政府與私人保險機構的措施，可能對我們產品或產品候選藥物的商業成功產生不利影響，甚至可能阻止其商業成功。
我們無法保證 Apraglutide 會獲得監管機構的批准，這是其能夠商業化所必需的步驟。
我們若無法成功開發並商業化其他產品候選藥物或已核准的產品，將影響我們的成長能力，並對我們的業務產生不利影響。
任何產品或產品候選藥物臨牀試驗完成的延遲，可能會導致成本增加，並延遲或限制我們產生收入的能力。
若 Apraglutide 及我們其他產品候選藥物獲得核准上市，其價格將部分取決於我們競爭對手所採用的價格與給付策略。
我們面臨競爭，可能有新產品出現，提供治療我們產品核准治療疾病的替代方案或更優良的選擇。
即使 linaclotide 已經獲准在美國及多個國家上市銷售，本公司或其合作夥伴仍可能無法取得在世界其他地區商業化 linaclotide 的許可。
若本公司無法成功與其他公司合作開發及商業化產品及/或產品候選藥物，將會影響本公司成長能力，並對本公司營運造成不利影響。
與 VectivBio 收購相關的風險
本公司可能無法實現 VectivBio 收購所預期的效益及預期的協同效應。
